title: Paklenica with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Park Rules, Costs
metaDescription: Dog-friendly Paklenica: the Kulina dog beach, leash rules in the national park, ferry rules, hotel dog fees, summer heat, vet basics and EU pet passport rules.
content:
## Does Paklenica have an official dog beach?

Yes, one. A designated dog beach sits on the east side of Kulina beach in Starigrad-Paklenica, near the Večka Kula tower. It is about a 20-minute walk from Camping Paklenica. Croatian designated dog areas usually have dog-waste bins, benches, running water and a dog shower, though the facilities at any one beach can be basic, so bring a bowl and fresh water.

The main beaches of the Paklenica Riviera are long, narrow pebble strips, and the sea is shallow and clear. Rules for dogs on the ordinary beaches are set locally and differ between stretches. Some pebble sections away from hotels and campsites are treated as tolerated for dogs, and signs mark the areas where dogs are not permitted. Keep the dog on a leash, collect waste, and follow any sign you see.

## Are dogs allowed on other beaches?

Across Croatia, beaches in front of hotels, campsites and lifeguarded sections are usually closed to dogs. Quieter public pebble stretches are often tolerated. A few other designated dog beaches exist on the Dalmatian coast, for example near Murter, but they are not close to Paklenica. Within Starigrad, the dog beach by Kulina is the dependable choice.

## Dogs in the old town and in restaurants

Starigrad-Paklenica is a linear seaside village with a waterfront promenade, not a walled old town. A dog on a leash can walk the whole promenade. The historic centre most visitors combine with Paklenica is Zadar, about 45 km southwest. Leashed dogs are generally seen on the old town streets there, but stone pavement gets very hot at midday, so walk early or in the evening.

Restaurants usually allow dogs on outdoor terraces, which is where most Starigrad konobas seat guests anyway. Inside, it is the owner's decision. Ask before sitting down, and keep the dog under the table.

## Dogs in Paklenica National Park

Most current sources say leashed dogs are allowed in Paklenica National Park. This covers the main Velika Paklenica canyon path, the best walk for a dog. It is flat to moderate, and the canyon walls give shade. The trail to the Paklenica mountain hut is about 12 km out and back and takes around 3.5–4 hours.

A few limits apply:

- Dogs must stay on a leash at all times, to protect wildlife and other hikers.
- Dogs wait outside Manita peć cave, which is visited in guided groups and has a fragile cave environment.
- Some sources claim dogs are banned entirely. Ask at the entrance booth when you buy your ticket, because rules can change.
- Climbing routes such as Anića kuk are not suitable with a dog.

Adult day tickets in 2026 cost €5 (January, February, November, December), €8 (March, April, October) and €10 (May–September). Children 7–18 and students pay less. Manita peć costs an extra €5, paid in cash. There is no separate dog fee.

The park is a short walk from the sea, so a morning in the canyon and an afternoon at the dog beach works well. Hike before 10:00 in summer.

## Dogs on ferries and catamarans

On Jadrolinija's local lines, pets travel free. Dogs must wear a muzzle and be on a leash. Dogs under 8 kg travel in a carrier of up to 45 x 35 x 25 cm, kept on your lap or under the seat. Larger dogs travel on the open deck of car ferries. On catamarans, larger dogs go in designated boxes on the open deck, for a fee and with a mandatory reservation. Book the box early in July and August, as spaces are limited. The Zadar islands are easily reached from Zadar, so check the line's rules before planning a day trip.

## What does accommodation charge for a dog?

Expect roughly €5–€15 per night in apartments and hotels, sometimes a flat cleaning fee instead, and sometimes nothing in private apartments. Always confirm the fee before booking.

Bluesun, the main operator in Starigrad-Paklenica, welcomes dogs. Hotels and holiday villages accept one dog up to 15 kg, and the number of dog rooms is limited, so tell them in advance. Camping Paklenica allows up to three dogs per pitch. Other pet-friendly places in Starigrad include Camp Sibuljina, Hotel Vicko and Bluesun Holiday Village Alan.

For a large dog, a campsite pitch or a ground-floor apartment with a garden is usually a better choice than a hotel room. Hotels with a 15 kg limit rule out most big dogs.

## Summer heat and best months

July and August often reach 30–35 °C, and pebbles and asphalt burn paws. Never leave a dog in a parked car. The best months are April to June and September to October. The sea is around 17 °C in spring and warms to the low 20s by September, and park tickets cost less. Strong bura wind can blow down the canyon, so a harness works better than a loose collar.

In July and August, skip the national park at midday. The long walk to the hut is not worth doing with a dog in the heat.

## Vet basics

The nearest full-service clinics are in Zadar, around 45 minutes by car. Pack tick and flea prevention, because ticks are common on grassy trails. Ask your own vet about sandfly protection for the Dalmatian coast. Bring spare medicine, and carry the vaccination record on your phone as well as on paper.

## EU pet passport rules for driving in

A dog entering Croatia from another EU country needs:

1. An ISO microchip, implanted before the rabies vaccination.
2. A valid rabies vaccination. In general, 21 days must pass after the first injection before travel.
3. An EU pet passport. Croatian vets issue them for €10.06 + VAT.

The EU framework changed on 22 April 2026, with Regulation 2026/131 replacing the previous 576/2013. Travellers' rules are almost unchanged and existing passports remain valid. Owners from non-EU countries should check the current residency rules for passports and health certificates. Checks at internal EU borders are rare since Croatia joined Schengen in 2023, but documents can be asked for at any time.

## Verdict: how dog-friendly is Paklenica?

Paklenica is dog-friendly, with caveats: 7 out of 10. The park admits leashed dogs on its main trail, there is a designated dog beach, and the campsites and hotels are used to pets. The limits are real: dogs cannot enter the cave, there is only one marked dog beach, and the heat in July and August makes midday outings hard. Visit in spring or autumn with a dog of any size and it is an excellent destination.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in Paklenica National Park?
faq.answer: Most current sources say yes, on a leash at all times, including on the Velika Paklenica canyon trail. Dogs are not allowed in Manita peć cave. Confirm at the entrance booth, because a few sources report a ban.

faq.question: Is there a dog beach in Starigrad-Paklenica?
faq.answer: Yes. The designated dog beach is on the east side of Kulina beach, near the Večka Kula tower. It is about a 20-minute walk from Camping Paklenica.

faq.question: Do dogs travel free on Croatian ferries?
faq.answer: On Jadrolinija's local car-ferry lines, pets travel free. Dogs need a leash and muzzle, and dogs over 8 kg stay on the open deck. Catamaran deck boxes for large dogs cost extra and must be reserved.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia from the EU?
faq.answer: A dog needs an ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport. A passport issued in Croatia costs €10.06 + VAT. The rabies shot should be at least 21 days old before travel.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Paklenica with a dog?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October are best, with mild temperatures and cheaper park tickets. July and August often reach 30–35 °C, which is too hot for long hikes and hot pebbles.

faq.question: How much does a hotel or apartment charge for a dog in Paklenica?
faq.answer: Expect about €5–€15 per night or a flat cleaning fee, and some private apartments charge nothing. Bluesun hotels take one dog up to 15 kg, and Camping Paklenica allows up to three dogs.

quickAnswer: Paklenica is moderately dog-friendly. Leashed dogs are generally allowed on the main canyon trail, there is a designated dog beach beside Kulina beach in Starigrad-Paklenica, and several campsites and hotels take dogs. Dogs are not allowed in Manita peć cave. Come in April–June or September–October, when it is cooler.
